subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first full-fledged Islamic commercial bank licence was issued in 2002 to:
explanation: The State Bank licensed Meezan Bank as the first dedicated Islamic commercial bank in 2002, reviving Islamic banking in Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan adopted a decimal currency, with 100 paisa to a rupee, in:
explanation: Decimal coinage was introduced on 1 January 1961, replacing the older system of annas and pice.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Pakistan Stock Exchange was formed in 2016 by merging the stock exchanges of:
explanation: The Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges were integrated into the single Pakistan Stock Exchange in January 2016.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which body regulates the stock market and corporate sector in Pakistan?
o: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
explanation: The SECP registers companies and regulates the capital market, insurance and non-bank financial companies.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s fiscal year runs from:
explanation: The federal and provincial budgets cover the fiscal year from 1 July to 30 June.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Federal Board of Revenue was formerly called the:
explanation: The Central Board of Revenue was reconstituted as the FBR under the Federal Board of Revenue Act 2007.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After the 18th Amendment, sales tax on services is collected in the provinces by:
explanation: Sales tax on services is a provincial subject, collected by bodies such as the Punjab Revenue Authority and Sindh Revenue Board.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the Constitution, tax on agricultural income is levied by the:
explanation: The federal list excludes agricultural income from federal income tax, so taxing it falls to the provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In Pakistan’s budget, the PSDP refers to:
o: the provincial share of federal taxes
explanation: The Public Sector Development Programme is the annual allocation for government development projects such as roads, dams and schools.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Pakistan Economic Survey is published every year by the:
explanation: The Finance Division releases the Economic Survey a day before the federal budget, reviewing the outgoing fiscal year.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Economic Coordination Committee of the Cabinet is normally chaired by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission
explanation: The ECC, a cabinet committee that takes day-to-day economic decisions, is headed by the Finance Minister.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s First Five-Year Plan covered the period:
explanation: The First Five-Year Plan (1955–60) was prepared by the Planning Board; the Second Plan (1960–65) under Ayub Khan was the most successful.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first federal budget was presented by:
explanation: As the first Finance Minister, Malik Ghulam Muhammad presented the budget for 1948–49 in February 1948.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan has been a member of the World Trade Organization since:
explanation: Pakistan, a GATT contracting party since 1948, became a founding member of the WTO when it was set up on 1 January 1995.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The European Union granted Pakistan GSP+ status in:
explanation: GSP+ took effect on 1 January 2014, giving many Pakistani exports duty-free access to the EU in return for implementing international conventions.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The China–Pakistan Free Trade Agreement was signed in:
explanation: The FTA was signed in November 2006 and came into force in 2007; its second phase was signed in 2019.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan became a member of the International Monetary Fund in:
explanation: Pakistan joined the IMF and the World Bank in July 1950.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan is a founding member of the Asian Development Bank, which was established in:
explanation: The ADB, headquartered in Manila, was established in 1966 with Pakistan among its founding members.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which rivers were given to India under the Indus Waters Treaty in 1960?
explanation: India received the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej), while Pakistan received the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by the:
explanation: The World Bank mediated nearly a decade of negotiations and is also a signatory to the treaty for specific purposes.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in the city of:
explanation: Nehru travelled to Karachi, then the capital, where the treaty was signed with Ayub Khan on 19 September 1960.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, each country appoints a commissioner to the:
explanation: The Permanent Indus Commission, with one commissioner from each side, exchanges data and tries to settle questions arising under the treaty.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Baglihar Dam, contested by Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty, is on the river:
explanation: Baglihar is an Indian run-of-river project on the Chenab in Jammu; Pakistan objected to features of its design.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Baglihar dispute (2005–07) was referred under the Indus Waters Treaty to a:
explanation: The World Bank appointed Swiss engineer Raymond Lafitte as Neutral Expert, who gave his decision in 2007.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In India, the Neelum River is known as the:
explanation: India’s Kishanganga project diverts water from this river before it enters Azad Kashmir as the Neelum, which led to a Court of Arbitration case.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The link canals built in Pakistan after the Indus Waters Treaty were designed to:
o: drain saline water into the sea
carry water from Pakistan to Afghanistan
carry water from the western rivers to areas once fed by the eastern rivers
explanation: Because the eastern rivers went to India, link canals transfer water from the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab to canals formerly fed by the Ravi and Sutlej.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Mangla and Tarbela dams were built under the:
explanation: The World Bank-administered Indus Basin Project financed Mangla, Tarbela, new barrages and link canals to replace the waters lost to India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Tarbela Dam is built on the river:
explanation: Tarbela, completed in 1976 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, impounds the Indus upstream of Attock.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Mangla Dam is built on the river:
explanation: Mangla, completed in 1967, was Pakistan’s first large storage dam and lies on the Jhelum.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Mangla Dam is located in the district of:
explanation: Mangla Dam and most of its reservoir lie in Mirpur district of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s largest hydroelectric power station is at:
explanation: Tarbela’s powerhouses, expanded through several extensions, have the largest installed hydel capacity in the country.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Warsak Dam is built on the:
explanation: Warsak Dam, completed in the early 1960s with Canadian help, lies on the Kabul River north-west of Peshawar.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being built on the river:
explanation: Diamer-Bhasha is a large storage dam on the Indus near Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Mohmand Dam is being built on the:
explanation: Mohmand Dam lies on the Swat River in Mohmand district, upstream of Peshawar, for flood control, irrigation and power.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The proposed Kalabagh Dam site is in the district of:
explanation: The long-disputed Kalabagh Dam would be built on the Indus at Kalabagh in Mianwali district, Punjab.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Hub Dam lies on the boundary between:
explanation: Hub Dam on the Hub River supplies water to Karachi and Lasbela and sits on the Sindh–Balochistan border.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Rawal Dam, a source of water for Rawalpindi and Islamabad, is on the:
explanation: Rawal Dam impounds the Korang River in the Margalla foothills; Simly Dam is on the Soan and Khanpur Dam on the Haro.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Neelum–Jhelum Hydropower Plant is located in:
explanation: The plant diverts the Neelum through a tunnel to a powerhouse near Muzaffarabad, returning the water to the Jhelum.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Dasu Hydropower Project is being built on the Indus in:
explanation: Dasu is a World Bank-supported run-of-river project on the Indus in Upper Kohistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Ghazi Barotha Hydropower Project uses water from the:
explanation: Ghazi Barotha diverts Indus water released from Tarbela through a power channel to Barotha before returning it to the river.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which of the following barrages is the oldest?
explanation: Sukkur Barrage was completed in 1932; Taunsa (1958), Kotri (1955) and Guddu (1962) were built after independence.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sukkur Barrage was originally named:
explanation: It was named after Sir George Lloyd, Governor of Bombay, who laid its foundation stone in 1923.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Kotri Barrage is also known as the:
explanation: Kotri Barrage near Hyderabad was completed in 1955 and named after Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Jinnah Barrage on the Indus is located at:
explanation: Jinnah Barrage near Kalabagh in Mianwali district feeds the Thal Canal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Guddu Barrage is located in the province of:
explanation: Guddu Barrage near Kashmore is the first barrage on the Indus in Sindh and also supplies canals reaching Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Marala Headworks near Sialkot is built on the river:
explanation: Marala Headworks on the Chenab feeds the Upper Chenab Canal and the Marala–Ravi link canal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kachhi Canal, taking off from Taunsa Barrage, is meant to irrigate land in:
explanation: The Kachhi Canal carries Indus water from Taunsa Barrage to the Dera Bugti and Kachhi plains of Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Karez, a system of underground channels for irrigation, is traditionally used in:
explanation: Karez tap groundwater at the foot of hills and carry it by gravity through tunnels, avoiding evaporation in Balochistan’s dry climate.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The SCARP projects launched in the 1960s were meant to control:
explanation: Salinity Control and Reclamation Projects installed tube-wells to lower water tables raised by canal seepage.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) was established in:
explanation: WAPDA was created in 1958 to develop water and power resources, and later built Mangla and Tarbela.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Water Apportionment Accord among the provinces was signed in:
explanation: The 1991 Accord fixed each province’s share of Indus waters and is still the basis of inter-provincial distribution.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which body was set up in 1992 to regulate the distribution of Indus waters among the provinces?
explanation: IRSA was created under an Act of 1992 to implement the Water Apportionment Accord of 1991.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first National Water Policy was approved in:
explanation: The Council of Common Interests approved the National Water Policy in April 2018.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Keenjhar Lake is a major source of drinking water for:
explanation: Keenjhar Lake in Thatta district, fed by the Indus through the Kalri Baghar feeder, supplies much of Karachi’s water.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Seawater intrusion into the Indus delta is mainly the result of:
o: reduced river flows below Kotri Barrage
explanation: With little fresh water passing Kotri for much of the year, the sea pushes into the delta, damaging land and mangroves.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the northern areas of Pakistan, the term GLOF refers to:
explanation: Glacial lake outburst floods occur when water dammed by ice or moraine suddenly breaks out, a growing hazard in Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Natural gas was first discovered in Pakistan in 1952 at:
explanation: The Sui field in Balochistan was discovered in 1952 and gave its name to the gas companies SNGPL and SSGC.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Sui gas field is located in the district of:
explanation: Sui lies in Dera Bugti district of Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Mari gas field is located in:
explanation: Mari gas field near Daharki in Ghotki district is one of Pakistan’s biggest gas producers.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sui Southern Gas Company distributes gas mainly in:
explanation: SSGC serves Sindh and Balochistan, while Sui Northern Gas Pipelines serves Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Oil was first struck in the area now forming Pakistan in 1915 at:
explanation: Attock Oil Company struck oil at Khaur in the Potohar region in 1915.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Attock Refinery is located at:
explanation: Attock Refinery at Morgah near Rawalpindi refines crude from the Potohar oilfields.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: PARCO’s Mid-Country Refinery is located at:
explanation: The Pak-Arab Refinery at Mahmoodkot in southern Punjab receives crude through a pipeline from Karachi.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Oil and Gas Development Corporation (now OGDCL) was set up in 1961 with the help of the:
explanation: OGDC was created in 1961 under a Soviet assistance agreement to explore Pakistan’s oil and gas.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan began importing liquefied natural gas (LNG) in:
explanation: The first LNG cargo arrived at the Port Qasim floating terminal in March 2015.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Iran–Pakistan gas pipeline is called the:
explanation: The Iran–Pakistan (originally Iran–Pakistan–India) gas project is popularly known as the Peace Pipeline.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The TAPI gas pipeline is planned to bring gas to Pakistan from:
explanation: TAPI (Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India) would carry gas from Turkmenistan’s Galkynysh field.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The CASA-1000 project is meant to supply Pakistan with electricity from:
explanation: CASA-1000 would transmit surplus summer hydropower from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan through Afghanistan to Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Thar coalfield is located in:
explanation: The huge Thar coal deposits lie beneath the desert of Tharparkar district in south-eastern Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Thar coal is mainly of which type?
explanation: Thar coal is low-rank lignite with high moisture, which is why it is burned in mine-mouth power plants.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lakhra coalfield is located in:
explanation: Lakhra near Khanote in Jamshoro district was long Sindh’s main working coalfield before Thar was developed.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first nuclear power plant, KANUPP, was built with the help of:
explanation: KANUPP, a Canadian CANDU-type reactor near Karachi, began operating in 1972.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Chashma nuclear power plants in Mianwali district were built with the cooperation of:
explanation: China supplied the Chashma units C-1 to C-4 under IAEA safeguards.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The K-2 and K-3 nuclear power units near Karachi use China’s reactor design called:
explanation: K-2 and K-3, commissioned in 2021 and 2022, were the first Hualong One reactors built outside China.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s nuclear power plants are operated by the:
explanation: PAEC builds and runs the nuclear power plants, while the Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority licenses and inspects them.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: NEPRA is the regulatory authority for:
explanation: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority issues licences and determines tariffs for the electricity sector.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which authority regulates the oil and gas sector in Pakistan?
explanation: The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority determines gas prices and licenses petroleum and CNG activities.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In Pakistan’s power sector, ‘circular debt’ refers to:
o: loans taken from the IMF for power projects
debt owed by provinces to the federal government
unpaid dues accumulating along the electricity supply chain
interest on Eurobonds issued for dams
explanation: When distribution companies and the government fail to pay in full, generators and fuel suppliers go unpaid, creating a chain of arrears.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Quaid-e-Azam Solar Park is located in:
explanation: The solar park stands in the Cholistan desert near Bahawalpur, one of the sunniest parts of Punjab.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Gharo–Jhimpir wind corridor is located in:
explanation: Strong coastal winds in Thatta district of Sindh host most of Pakistan’s wind farms.
